card.law_is_about: Revising building-energy and heating rules, including tenant cost allocation.
card.they_want: A technology-neutral heating-cost cap and stronger tenant protection.
card.they_claim: The population share meeting a low/lower-middle-income energy-poverty definition rose from 14.5% to 25.2%.
card.the_problem: Those figures belong to the cited study’s broader measure without that income restriction.

counter_quote.translation_en: Translation: In 2021 the rate rose slightly to 11.3%, before climbing to 16.8% in the current year.

locator.paragraph: Left column, paragraph explicitly discussing the third definition.

correction: Keep the measures separate: IW definition 1 uses energy spending above 10% of net household income, without an income restriction; definition 3 adds relative poverty/lower-middle income. Its overall population shares are 11.3%/16.8%, rather than definition 1’s 14.5%/25.2%. These are modelled 2021/2022 estimates without relief packages; the body uses persons, while the headline says households. Neither is a within-low-income-group incidence rate.
effect: The narrower-income vulnerability statistic is overstated relative to the cited measure, weakening this introductory support for the requested cost protection.
limits: The study finds increasing risk under every definition. The issue does not establish current hardship, the correct household-weighted rate, or whether a heating-cost cap is desirable. A benign reading takes the income phrase as a broad description of especially vulnerable groups; its placement as an explanatory definition makes that less natural. No intent is inferred.
materiality_explanation: Minor editorial judgment: a substantial difference in the cited subgroup measure, but an introductory supporting statistic rather than a cost estimate or central mechanism of the proposed cap.
direction_explanation: Using the broader, higher share for the narrower vulnerable group strengthens the protection argument. This direction is separate from severity.

confidence.text_source_mismatch: high for the two measures; the strength of the definitional reading is interpretive
